Title: Verify order details and QR code display correctly after order creation
Preconditions: User has just completed creating a new order with customer details, items, and photos. The order includes an advance payment and a due amount.
Steps:
1. Complete the order creation process by confirming all details and submitting the order. 2. Observe the success page that loads automatically after submission. 3. Verify the order ID displayed at the top of the page. 4. Check the customer name, order date, delivery date, and trial date. 5. Confirm the total amount, paid amount (advance), and due amount are displayed correctly. 6. Verify the QR code is displayed and scannable.

Test Data: Order ID: auto-generated (e.g., '1-20240515-0001'), Customer Name: 'John Doe', Order Date: today's date, Delivery Date: tomorrow's date, Trial Date: two days from today, Total Amount: 2000, Paid Amount: 500, Due Amount: 1500
Expected Result: The success page displays the correct order ID, customer name, dates, and monetary values formatted as currency (e.g., '2,000.00'). The QR code is visible and can be scanned without errors. All details match the order submitted.

Title: Verify order dates are displayed in a consistent format regardless of input format
Section: Order Success Page - Date Format Handling
Preconditions: User has just completed creating a new order. The order date was stored in 'YYYYMMDD' format (e.g., '20240515').
Steps:
1. Complete the order creation process and navigate to the success page. 2. Observe the order date displayed on the success page. 3. Verify the date is shown in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format (e.g., '2024-05-15').

Test Data: Order Date: '20240515' (stored as 'YYYYMMDD')
Expected Result: The order date is displayed in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format (e.g., '2024-05-15') on the success page.

Title: Verify monetary values are displayed with consistent decimal formatting
Section: Order Success Page - Monetary Value Formatting
Preconditions: User has just completed creating a new order with monetary values that may include whole numbers or decimals.
Steps:
1. Complete the order creation process and navigate to the success page. 2. Observe the total amount, paid amount, and due amount displayed. 3. Verify all monetary values show exactly two decimal places (e.g., '2000.00', '500.00').

Test Data: Total Amount: 2000, Paid Amount: 500, Due Amount: 1500
Expected Result: All monetary values are displayed with two decimal places (e.g., '2,000.00', '500.00', '1,500.00'). No values are truncated or missing decimals.
